question_stem:
An $\alpha$-particle moves in a straight line through a vacuum with a constant speed of $4.1 \times 10^6 \text{m s}^{-1}$. The $\alpha$-particle enters a uniform electric field at point $A$, as shown in Fig. 4.1.

{{figure:figure_4_1}}

Fig. 4.1

The $\alpha$-particle continues to move in the same straight line until it is brought to rest at point $B$ by the electric field. The deceleration of the $\alpha$-particle by the electric field is $2.7 \times 10^{14} \text{m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State the direction of the electric field.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
The $\alpha$-particle is at point $A$ at time $t = 0$.

On Fig. 4.2, sketch the variation with time $t$ of the momentum of the $\alpha$-particle as it travels from point $A$ to point $B$. Numerical values are not required.

{{figure:figure_4_2}}

Fig. 4.2

parts.label: (e)
parts.text: State the name of the quantity that is represented by the gradient of the graph in (d).

parts.label: (f)(i)
parts.part_stem: A $\beta^-$ particle now enters the electric field along the same initial path as the $\alpha$-particle and with the same initial speed of $4.1 \times 10^6 \text{m s}^{-1}$.
parts.text: Calculate the kinetic energy, in J, of the $\beta^-$ particle at point $A$.

parts.label: (f)(ii)
parts.text: State and explain the differences between the electric force on the $\beta^-$ particle in the electric field and the electric force on the $\alpha$-particle in the electric field.

parts.label: (f)(iii)
parts.text: The $\beta^-$ particle is produced by the decay of a nucleus. State the name of another lepton that is produced at the same time as the $\beta^-$ particle.
